title: Introduce stochastic probe multiplexer for tail regression isolation
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: existing canary probes rely on fixed synthetic inputs or direct traffic shadowing which can either overfit to synthetic patterns or perturb production routing. This PR implements a 'stochastic probe multiplexer' (SPM) as a lightweight probe layer that interleaves randomized virtual probes with low-impact production-shaped sampling to isolate rare tail regressions and reduce probe-to-prod mismatch. Goals: 1) improve sensitivity to tail latency/throughput regressions without raising false positives from synthetic-only probes, 2) avoid meaningful interference with production traffic and SLOs, 3) produce richer feature vectors for the canary evaluator to support quorum-based rollback decisions. What this change does (summary): - Adds a new probe coordination service (perf/canary/probe_mux.py) that defines virtual probe streams, randomized offsets, and multiplexing policies. - Implements sampling kernels that shape virtual probe payloads to observed traffic histograms (perf/canary/sampler.py). - Integrates multiplexed probe signals with the canary evaluator (perf/canary/evaluator.rs bindings updated) so that probe-origin metadata is preserved end-to-end. - Adds permutation-test based anomaly scoring and a quorum gate to the canary decision logic (perf/canary/quorum_gate.py). - Dashboard and alerting updates (dashboards/canary_probe_mux.yaml) and lightweight synthetic fixtures for CI (tests/probe_mux_test.py). Backwards compatibility & safety: SPM runs disabled by default. When enabled for a canary rollout, it respects per-customer rate caps and can be configured in the rollout policy (default: <0.1% of requests as virtual probes, randomized across zones). The module supports 'dry-run' mode to surface signals to observability without affecting routing. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed with SRE and evaluator team (ENG-1879) - [x] Unit + integration tests added and passing - [x] Feature flag gated and opt-in via rollout policy - [x] Dashboard and alerting updated - [x] Load safety checks (per-zone rate caps) implemented Performance notes: Initial lab runs on a 48-GPU perf bench with mixed short/long sequences show 2-4% improvement in detection time for injected tail regressions at equivalent false positive rates versus the existing synthetic-probe baseline. See perf results in the commits. Rollout plan: start as opt-in on internal canary clusters for 2 weeks, then gradually enable on canaries with high variance workloads. Related: references SUP-4421 incident postmortem where single-shot synthetic probes missed a multi-modal tail shift. Risks & mitigations: randomization increases complexity in debug — all probes include canonical trace ids and probe descriptors; dry-run mode avoids routing changes; quorum gate favors conservative rollback thresholds by default.
